title: aborting a document load does not abort ongoing navigation of descendant navigables
body:
When new navigation https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigate begins I would expect ongoing navigations of navigable itself and all descendant navigables to be aborted. This happens for a navigable itself in step 17:
> [Set the ongoing navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-ongoing-navigation) for navigable to navigationId.

And for descendants it is supposed to happen in step 20.3:
> [Queue a global task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#queue-a-global-task) on the [navigation and traversal task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigation-and-traversal-task-source) given navigable's [active window](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#nav-window) to [abort](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#abort-a-document) navigable's [active document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#nav-document).

but document abortion procedure (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#abort-a-document) doesn't set ongoing navigation of a navigable to null. Instead it changes navigation id of a document to null .

> Set document's [navigation id](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-navigation-id) to null.

Is that what actually supposed to happen or there is a mistake and it should be "ongoing navigation" of a navigable instead?

A note in the spec clarifies:
> This will have the effect of aborting any ongoing navigations of navigable, since at certain points during navigation, changes to the [ongoing navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigation) will cause further work to be abandoned.

but changing navigation id of a document doesn't seem to abort subsequent navigation work.

@domenic
